hook.line: When everybody already knows about a problem, nobody wants to explain it again. Spanish packs the whole matter into two small words.
hook.es: Lo de la reunión me tiene preocupado.
hook.en: The meeting thing has me worried. (a man speaking)

examples.es: Lo de la reunión me tiene preocupado.
examples.en: The meeting thing has me worried. (a man speaking)
How's the new job thing going?

examples.es: Lo de ayer fue un error.
examples.en: What happened yesterday was a mistake.

examples.es: Siento mucho lo de doña Rosa.
examples.en: I'm so sorry about what happened with Doña Rosa.
What happened with the Altamira business?

rule:
*Lo de* plus a noun means "the matter of…", something you and the listener already know about. English has no single word for it, so it says "the … thing", "that business" or "what happened with…".

*Lo* never changes for gender or number: *lo de la reunión*, *lo de los papeles*. With *el*, *de* and *el* join: *lo del trabajo*.

It only works with shared context. If the listener has no idea, spell it out.
smallPrint: Teachers call *lo* here the neuter article. It turns a whole situation into something you can talk about.

readAndPick.es: Lo de la reunión me tiene preocupado.
options: The meeting thing has me worried. (a man speaking)
The meeting thing has me worried. (a woman speaking)
The meetings worry him.
Where is the new job?
Who has the new job?
How's the new job thing going?

readAndPick.es: Lo de ayer fue un error.
options: Yesterday I made a mistake.
What happened yesterday was a mistake.
Yesterday was a holiday.

readAndPick.es: Siento mucho lo de doña Rosa.
options: I really like Doña Rosa.
I miss Doña Rosa's café.
I'm so sorry about what happened with Doña Rosa.
What happened with the Altamira business?
Who is Altamira?
Where is Altamira?

readAndPick.es: Lo de la beca sigue pendiente.
options: The scholarship was awarded last week.
The scholarship matter is still pending.
The scholarships are still pending.

readAndPick.es: Lo del apartamento ya está listo.
options: The apartment is far away.
The apartments are ready.
The apartment matter is already sorted.

readAndPick.es: Hablamos de lo del contrato mañana.
options: We'll talk about the contract matter tomorrow.
We talked about the contract yesterday.
We'll talk to the contract tomorrow.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *Lo de* or *La de* and type the whole sentence: *___ ayer fue un error.*
yourTurn.answer: Lo de ayer fue un error.
accept: Lo de ayer fue un error
yourTurn.why: *Lo* is neutral, so it never takes *la*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: How's the scholarship thing going?
accept: Cómo va lo de la beca
yourTurn.why: *Lo de* plus *la beca* packs the whole matter into the question.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I'm so sorry about what happened with Doña Rosa.
yourTurn.answer: Siento mucho lo de doña Rosa.
accept: Siento mucho lo de doña Rosa
yourTurn.why: *Lo de* plus a name points to what happened to that person.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: What happened with the Altamira business?
accept: Qué pasó con lo de Altamira
yourTurn.why: After *con*, *lo de* still means "the matter of".

yourTurn.prompt: Swap the topic to the contract (*de* and *el* join into *del*): *Lo de la reunión me tiene preocupado.*
yourTurn.answer: Lo del contrato me tiene preocupado.
accept: Lo del contrato me tiene preocupado
yourTurn.why: *De* plus *el* becomes *del*, and *lo* stays the same.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The apartment matter is already sorted.
yourTurn.answer: Lo del apartamento ya está listo.
accept: Lo del apartamento ya está listo
yourTurn.why: *Lo del* plus a noun is the whole matter, and *listo* stays masculine.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Thanks for yesterday.
yourTurn.why: *Lo de ayer* covers everything that happened yesterday.

pitfalls.wrong: La de la reunión me tiene preocupado.
pitfalls.right: Lo de la reunión me tiene preocupado.
pitfalls.why: Almost. It is not a feminine noun; *lo* is the neutral "matter", even before *la reunión*.

pitfalls.wrong: ¿Cómo va lo de el trabajo nuevo?
Lo sobre la reunión me tiene preocupado.
pitfalls.right: Lo de la reunión me tiene preocupado.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Spanish links the matter with *de*, not with *sobre*.

personal: What is one ongoing matter in your life that people around you know about? Type a sentence about it with *lo de*.
